evidence: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:14 totalPages = Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1. With user_count=50, limit=50 this gives 2 pages when only 1 exists (and 100/50 gives 3). showingLast (line 18) compares currentPage == totalPages, so the 'next' button stays enabled on the real last page and leads to an empty page. Math.ceil(user_count/limit) is correct.

admin-group.js.es6:32 clamps the offset with Math.min(offset+limit, user_count), so an offset equal to user_count is allowed, and group.js findMembers clamps to user_count the same way. The empty page only appears because the showingLast guard is wrong (issue 0): with totalPages fixed, next() is never called on the last page and offset+limit < user_count always holds. Clamping to (totalPages-1)*limit adds defense in depth, but the root cause is issue 0.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 usernames.split(',') has no strip, and User.find_by_username (app/models/user.rb:175) only downcases, so ' bob' would not match. Blank entries return nil and are skipped harmlessly. The UI does not produce whitespace: user-selector.js.es6:52 does items.join(','). Only API callers are affected. Adding strip and reject(&:blank?) is cheap hardening.

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-23 limit=(params[:limit]||50).to_i and offset=params[:offset].to_i with no bounds. This is a public (non-admin) endpoint, so ?limit=1000000 on a large automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0) loads and serializes every user, and a negative limit or offset raises a PG error (500). The previous code had a 200 cap for automatic groups. posts_controller.rb:301-302 already uses the clamping convention [offset,0].max and [limit,100].min.

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:113 uses 'xhr :put, :remove_member' for the automatic-group case, but the route is 'delete members' (config/routes.rb:49) and the sibling test at line 124 uses :delete. Controller specs dispatch straight to the action, so the test passes but is inconsistent and does not document the real verb. This is a test-quality nit, not a production bug.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:1 guards on {{#if model}} but line 6 iterates {{#each m in members}}. The route (routes/group-members.js.es6) now sets the model and calls findMembers() without waiting, so the model is always truthy and the 'last seen' header renders with no rows while loading, or permanently for an empty group. The effect is cosmetic, and guarding on members would remove it.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:19 has a '' inside the {{#each}} after '' with no matching '
' opening tag, which is invalid markup inside . It already existed before this PR, but the PR edits this template (line 6), and the one-line removal is trivial.

config/routes.rb:49-50 declares 'delete "members"' and 'put "members"' directly inside 'resources :groups do' with no 'member do' block. Rails treats routes declared this way as nested routes, so they generate /admin/groups/:group_id/members with param :group_id. That is what Admin::GroupsController#add_members/#remove_member use via params.require(:group_id), and group.js calls '/admin/groups/'+id+'/members.json'. The params match.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:472,474 hardcode color #333/#aaa with !important for .next/.previous. The same file uses theme variables elsewhere ($primary at line 29, $tertiary at line 58, scale-color-diff()), so on dark color schemes these links would be low-contrast. A few other hardcoded colors already exist (lines 1382, 1387), so this is a consistency and theming improvement, not a break.

admin-group.js.es6:61-65 addMembers calls model.addMembers(usernames) but never resets this.usernames. The author's own '// TODO: should clear the input' comment on line 62 acknowledges this. Re-adding is harmless server-side but is a UX papercut; setting usernames to '' in the promise .then would fix it.
